correctness.rationale: Normalized probability coefficients a_{k,n}=[z^n] exp(lambda sum_{j=1}^k z^j) obey n a_{k,n}=lambda sum_{j<=min(k,n)} j a_{k,n-j}, and are strictly increasing for n>0. Independently executed exact Fraction recurrence at B=q/10^6 and L=B-10^-6 for all 14 k values, n<=40k; every target crosses one and all alternate coefficients are strictly below one at B, kB<4. For n>40k every summand needs >=41 jumps, giving a_n(B)<=sum_{m>=41}(kB)^m/m!<2*4^41/41!<1. Thus all infinitely many indices and all real lambda before first crossing are controlled, with no possible third tie. The smallest alternate gap at k=15 is at n=26, about 0.000528; no significance is attributed to decimals as proofs.

value.rationale: An exact global proof of a previously reported but numerically unsupported first exception is a motivated open certification problem for a natural probability-law modal transition. It settles the order-15 first transition, its precise unique equality case and true infinite-support cutoff, without pretending that previously published numerical values were newly discovered. Meaningful finite-order result; not a mere table recomputation because rigorous exclusion of every index and tie is missing from the strongest prior numerical studies.

final_claim: For first global-mode transitions of order-k Poisson with iid Poisson jumps, 2<=k<=14 have exactly the tied modes {0,k}, while k=15 has exactly {0,25}; an explicit rational recurrence certificate and an infinite-tail estimate prove uniqueness and strict millionth root intervals. The k=15 numerical phenomenon was observed by Mane in 2023, not discovered here.
